title: Home
slide0_body: You do not have to answer questions about your immigration status. Say: "I am exercising my right to remain silent."
slide1_body: Do not open the door for ICE unless they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge. Ask them to slide it under the door.
slide2_body: You have the right to speak with a lawyer before answering questions. Do not sign any documents without legal counsel.
h1b_desc: For workers in specialty occupations like tech, engineering, and finance. Requires a U.S. employer sponsor. Valid for 3 years, extendable to 6.
h2a_desc: For temporary agricultural workers. Allows foreign nationals to work on U.S. farms during peak seasons.
l1_desc: For employees transferring within the same company from a foreign office to a U.S. office. Requires at least 1 year of employment.
f1_desc: For full-time academic students at accredited U.S. colleges or universities. Allows limited on-campus work and OPT after graduation.
j1_desc: For exchange visitors including students, interns, teachers, and researchers in approved programs.
m1_desc: For vocational and non-academic students. Covers trade schools, culinary programs, and flight academies.
b2_desc: For tourism, vacation, visiting family, or medical treatment. Typically allows a stay of up to 6 months.
b1_desc: For business visitors attending meetings or conferences. Does not allow you to work for a U.S. employer.
esta_desc: Citizens of 40+ countries can visit the U.S. for up to 90 days without a visa. Must apply online before travel.
family_desc: For immediate relatives of U.S. citizens including spouses, unmarried children under 21, and parents.
workgc_desc: For workers with job offers from U.S. employers. Divided into preference categories EB-1 through EB-5.
refugee_desc: Refugees and asylees who have been in the U.S. for at least one year may apply for permanent residency.
lottery_desc: Each year 55,000 green cards are available through a random lottery to people from countries with low U.S. immigration rates.
e1_title: If ICE Comes to Your Door
e1_body: Do not open the door. Ask if they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge. An administrative warrant does not give them the right to enter your home.
e2_body: You do not have to answer any questions. Clearly say: "I am exercising my right to remain silent." This applies to everyone regardless of immigration status.
e3_body: You have the right to speak with a lawyer. Do not sign any documents before speaking to one. Ask for a free legal aid organization if you cannot afford one.
e4_body: Stay calm and keep your hands visible. You are not required to answer questions about your immigration status.
offices_desc: Find immigration offices and legal aid organizations near you.
